correctness.rationale: The two binary transitions on (B_n(−2),B_{n+1}(−2)) have determinant −2, a unit at every odd m, so primitivity is invariant. Multiplying the displayed matrices verifies P^{-1}(AB^{-1})²P=E_{12}(−4) and P^{-1}A(AB^{-1})²A^{-1}P=E_{21}(−2). These yield all shears; local-ring elimination and CRT generate SL₂, including at repeated prime powers. A primitive pair extends to a determinant-one basis, so transitivity is on exactly the primitive pairs. The positive-word orbit equals the group orbit by finiteness. The two transitions are permutations and the accessible (0,1) has an A-self-loop; the walk thus mixes to uniform. The prefix-cylinder argument bounds discrepancies of cylinders of free length ≥L by their total size times the uniform mixing error and treats shorter cylinders by a total size <2^L, proving natural density at arbitrary endpoints. CRT counts the marginal fibers as stated. A fresh direct recurrence and BFS over m=3,9,25,27,45,75,125 through a prefix of 65,536 checked the exact orbit sizes 8,72,600,648,1728,4800,15000 and all marginal fiber sizes. Prefix frequencies were finite corroboration, not an exact density test; replay: branches/9b74cb2e-5a23-415a-abcb-70fa0f5af4a2/independent_check.py.

evidence: Theorem 2.2 gives natural density as the fraction of reachable states accepted by a finite automaton with invertible digits and a zero digit fixing the initial state. Ulas–Ulas show consecutive polynomial coprimality; Gawron analyzes other rational evaluations via finite automata.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader invertible-automaton theorem applies to the frozen transitions from (0,1), but requires as input the reachable states. Starting at (0,1) is legitimate since A fixes it and B sends it to (1,−2). Invertibility ensures preserved primitivity but does not imply transitivity; the specialization-specific group argument is necessary.

originality.rationale: Deshouillers–Schinzel already prove the density mechanism for invertible digit automata, and their Stern result at t=1 has exactly the same form. The supported distinct result is reachability of the full primitive orbit for the t=−2 generators at every odd modulus, via the opposite shears, and hence the law for that specialization. The inspected earlier primitive-orbit proof uses different generators and does not supply this input.
residual_risks: A general theorem identifying the orbit for a larger family of Stern-polynomial specializations could cover −2; no such decisive statement was verified in the inspected sources.
The ordinary-Stern law already covers the identical recurrence modulo three, and automaton uniformity itself is not new.

value.rationale: The orbit calculation gives a complete exact modular law at a natural nonordinary specialization with invertible odd-modulus digits. It resolves all composite odd moduli, including repeated prime factors, and supplies exact scalar densities that are not all equal. The opposite-unit-shear argument explains why full primitive support holds uniformly rather than just displaying frequencies in small moduli.
